annotations.title: General Assembly Adopts Resolution Calling upon States Not to Recognize Changes in Status of Crimea Region | Meetings Coverage and Press Releases

content.text:
**Under international law and according to most countries: no — Crimea does not belong to Russia.** Crimea is internationally recognized as part of **Ukraine**, and Russia’s 2014 annexation is widely treated as illegal or invalid.

**In practice:** Russia has controlled Crimea since 2014 and treats it as part of the Russian Federation. But the UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity and called on states not to recognize changes to Crimea’s status after the 2014 referendum; the UN and U.S. continue to describe Crimea as occupied Ukrainian territory. ([press.un.org](https://press.un.org/en/2014/ga11493.doc.htm?utm_source=openai))

So the short answer is: **de jure Crimea is Ukrainian; de facto it is under Russian control.**
